answer: A sybil-resistant economy binds each identity to multiple hard factors - a funded stake, a verified device, and an irreplaceable operator - so one human cannot spawn a vine of lookalikes without paying each branch. Attacking an island of honest agents then costs more than it captures, and reputation earned through real work cannot be transferred to a fresh clone. A saffron-marked public proof of uniqueness makes the cheapest fake still unprofitable, shifting the attacker's tradeoff toward honesty.
